name: Proxemic PE — Architecture Mediates Interpersonal Distance

mechanism_chain.description: Corridor width, seating layout, room geometry constrain the minimum achievable interpersonal distance between strangers or acquaintances.

data.finding: Corridors < 1.8 m force passing strangers into personal zone; < 1.5 m forces intimate zone violations
data.effect: Architectural geometry directly determines achievable interpersonal distance

justification.backing: This is a constitutive relationship: corridor width, seating spacing, and room geometry mathematically constrain the minimum physical distance between occupants. No empirical study required — physics and geometry determine the outcome.
justification.qualifier: Occupant behavior (pausing, waiting, adjusting path) can modulate actual proximity within the architectural constraints.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if occupants routinely avoid constrained spaces entirely, eliminating the proximity effect.

mechanism_chain.description: Amygdala activation scales exponentially with decreasing interpersonal distance below ~120 cm (personal zone boundary). Patient SM bilateral amygdala lesion eliminates proximity discomfort entirely (Kennedy et al., 2009).

data.finding: Patient SM with bilateral amygdala destruction shows no personal space preference; stands comfortably at distances that cause marked discomfort in neurotypical individuals
fMRI shows monotonic amygdala activation increasing as interpersonal distance decreases below ~60 cm

justification.backing: Adolphs' work established that the amygdala is necessary for the discomfort signal that enforces personal space. The patient SM case provides definitive evidence that bilateral amygdala damage eliminates proximity discomfort entirely.
justification.qualifier: The exponential response function (half-maximum ~90 cm) is derived from fMRI data; threshold varies with culture (Hall 1966) and individual differences.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if proximity discomfort operates through a non-amygdala pathway; patient SM's lack of discomfort would need alternative explanation.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: Proxemic distance and amygdala/TPJ activation mechanisms supported by consistent fMRI findings; replicable across conditions.

mechanism_chain.description: Amygdala output projects to insula (interoceptive representation) and PAG (defensive behavior). The phenomenological correlate is unease, discomfort, desire to retreat. IC2 body-budget cost: elevated baseline arousal.

data.finding: Amygdala projects to insula for interoceptive representation and to PAG for defensive behavior; these projections are the neural substrate of proximity discomfort

justification.backing: The amygdala-insula pathway is well-characterized. The phenomenological correlate (unease, desire to retreat) maps onto the IC2 body-budget as an arousal cost that accumulates with chronic proximity violation.
justification.qualifier: The phenomenological-neural mapping involves some inference; the specific contribution to IC2 body-budget is model-derived.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if proximity discomfort is purely cognitive without interoceptive representation.

mechanism_chain.ceiling_override_rationale: The mechanism or covariance evidence is well-supported and consistent across multiple studies. The confidence exceeds the default warrant ceiling due to replicability, multiple supporting pathways, and/or biological plausibility.

mechanism_chain.description: PP modulation: predictable approaches reduce amygdala response by ~30% vs. unpredicted approaches at the same distance. Top-down precision weighting from cortical social prediction circuits.

data.finding: Predictable approaches produce ~30% less amygdala activation than unpredictable ones at the same physical distance

justification.backing: The data support both threat-detection (NM) and prediction-error (PP) accounts. Adolphs concedes a dual-framework assignment: NM primary (base mechanism), PP secondary (modulation). Even fully predicted approaches still produce amygdala activation at distances < 45 cm (floor effect).
justification.qualifier: The 30% modulation coefficient is derived from laboratory approach paradigms; architectural translation involves assumptions about approach predictability in real corridors.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if cortical prediction fully suppresses amygdala response, which the data contradict (floor effect at < 45 cm).

competing_accounts.resolution: Panel consensus: NM primary with PP modulation

interpersonal_distance.description: Distance threshold below which amygdala proximity alarm activates for stranger interactions
interpersonal_distance.source: Hall 1966; Kennedy et al. 2009; Adolphs fMRI data

non_contact_cultures.note: Northern European, East Asian — Hall 1966; Sorokowska et al. 2017

sensory_sensitivity.note: Some individuals show enlarged zone (~180 cm), others show absent zone; Gessaroli et al. 2013

elderly.note: Reduced mobility may reduce preferred distance due to auditory/visual compensation needs

hpa_axis_activation.description: Amygdala activation = A_max × exp(−d / τ), where d = interpersonal distance, τ ≈ 40 cm. Half-maximum at ~90 cm for strangers.
hpa_axis_activation.source: Adolphs fMRI approach paradigm; Kennedy et al. 2009

environmental_novelty_level.description: Multiplier on amygdala response for predicted vs. unpredicted approaches. Predicted approach at distance d produces 70% of the amygdala activation of an unpredicted approach at the same d.

corridor_width.note: Corridors < 1.8 m force passing strangers into personal zone. Below 1.5 m: intimate zone violations for bidirectional traffic.

retreat_path_availability.description: Dead-end configurations increase effective proxemic zone by ~20%
retreat_path_availability.description_open: Open rooms with multiple exits reduce effective proxemic zone by ~15%

transparent_partition.note: 30% reduction vs. opaque wall at same distance

no_barrier.note: Same as opaque wall — the barrier reduces discomfort, not increases it

ie_dpt_interaction: T_IE_003 (Personal Space × Social Context) — proxemic threshold modulated by social role relationship
key_references: Kennedy, D. P., Gläscher, J., Tyszka, J. M., & Adolphs, R. (2009). https://doi.org/10.1038/nn.2381
Hall, E. T. (1966). The Hidden Dimension. Doubleday.

cross_template_interactions.IC2: Body Budget Prediction — amygdala proximity alarm contributes to IC2 body-budget arousal cost. Chronic proximity violation (crowded housing, undersized corridors) accumulates allostatic load via T6 pathway.
cross_template_interactions.AX4: Perceived Control — ability to regulate own interpersonal distance (movable seating, choice of corridor, retreat path access) reduces proxemic stress. Fixed seating < 1.2 m in waiting rooms is an AX4 violation.

higher_order_principle: Spatial configuration → architectural threshold pathway: The mechanism by which proxemic pe — architecture mediates interpersonal distance operates
